stem: Why are textured ground tiles with raised domes installed along train platform edges and street crosswalks?

options.text: To warn cyclists and scooter riders, through a raised surface, that they are approaching a vehicle lane.
options.rationale: Tactile warning surfaces alert pedestrians who are blind; they are not a cyclist or scooter lane marking.

options.text: To guide passengers toward ticket machines and information desks through a distinct floor texture.
options.rationale: The raised domes mark a hazard boundary; they do not provide directional guidance to station facilities.

options.text: To mark the area where pedestrians should wait before crossing through a change in floor texture.
options.rationale: The domes mark the boundary of the roadway or platform edge, not a designated waiting area.

options.text: To alert people who are blind, with a cane or underfoot, to a drop-off or roadway boundary.
options.rationale: Detectable warning surfaces alert cane users and individuals with vision loss that they are approaching an edge or street crossing.

explanation: Tactile ground surface indicators (such as raised domes or bars) provide underfoot and cane-detectable tactile warnings. They notify travelers with visual disabilities of impending drop-offs, transit edges, and vehicular roadway transitions.
